# How to Fill Kids Classes: 7 Practical Steps for Southern California Studios and Camps

Filling kids' classes comes down to seven habits: price clearly, discount only the seats about to expire, write listings that answer parents' real questions, run a waitlist, reply fast, show up where families already browse, and read your numbers. On ORYN Quest, joining costs $0 today with nothing taken from the price you set, and each step below pairs one platform feature with the plain practice that makes it work.

## 1. Set a Dollar Price Per Seat and Let the Platform Round Up to Credits

In the listing form, the price field is labeled "the dollar amount you receive per booked seat." You set a dollar price, the platform converts it to credits for families by rounding up, and you are paid exactly your dollar price. At today's rate, a $20 class shows families 23 credits, and the vendor receives $20.00.

Two practical notes follow from that setup. First, discounting never cuts your pay: promo codes, last-minute deals, and the sibling discount are paid for by ORYN, not out of your price. Second, families see only credits at checkout, so keep pricing decisions in the listing form rather than in chat.

How do you choose the number? Price for your local market, not your costs alone. A sensory-friendly gymnastics class in Pasadena with small ratios can sit well above the going rate for a large group class in the same ZIP, because parents pay for fit. Walk through your own neighborhood as a parent would: check what comparable classes charge, look at what your competitors include at that price, and round to a clean number. For broader demand tactics, our guide on [how to get more students for your kids' classes](https://orynquest.com/blog/how-to-get-more-students-for-kids-classes) goes deeper than pricing alone.

## 2. Switch On the Last-Minute Deal for Seats Within 24 Hours

Empty seats within 24 hours of a session are the hardest kind to fill, and a seat that goes unfilled earns nothing. A last-minute deal lets you offer 5 to 75% off sessions starting within 24 hours that still have open seats, and ORYN pays the discount. You still receive your full dollar price per seat.

The sweet spot is a moderate discount on classes that would otherwise run with gaps: a swim session with three open lanes, an art class with spare easels, a camp day with unfilled spots. If the class fills at full price, no deal exists. The discount only applies to seats that would have earned you nothing anyway.

Time the deal for when parents are actually deciding. Late-afternoon and evening browsing, and Sunday-night planning for the week ahead, are when parents scramble for next-day plans. If your sessions run weekday mornings, a deal published the prior evening has the longest runway. For the fuller playbook on moving empty inventory without touching your list price, see [how to fill open spots in a kids' class without discounting](https://orynquest.com/blog/how-to-fill-open-spots-in-a-kids-class).

## 3. Build a Listing That Tells Parents Everything They Need to Decide
![A parent and young child stand together near the entrance of a sunny Southern California community center](/blog-assets/how-to-fill-a-kids-class-in-2026-5-booking-page-changes-that-s1.jpg)


Parents of children ages 3 to 12 book when they can answer three questions in under a minute: Is this right for my child's age? Can we get there and park? Will my child be comfortable? Fill in the optional fields that answer those questions: age range, skill level, total seats, and accessibility accommodations. Many Southern California families specifically search for sensory-friendly and autism-friendly options, so stating your accommodations plainly reaches families who otherwise scroll past.

Photos do more heavy lifting than any paragraph. Show children mid-activity, faces engaged, space visible. A studio photo with real kids in it outsells a stock image of a spotless empty room, because parents read an empty room as an empty class. Google's own guidance on image search results notes that page and image context drive whether an image gets used, so put descriptive captions around your listing images. Aim for the full five photos: one wide shot of the space, two of activities in progress, one of the instructor engaging kids, and one that shows arrival or parking.

Add access and parking info even if it feels obvious. What is obvious to you, who drives there daily, is a decision point for a parent juggling two kids and a 4 p.m. window. Mention the things parents quietly worry about: where they park, whether siblings can wait nearby, what the drop-off handoff looks like. If the written parts stall you, our post on [writing a kids' class listing parents actually book](https://orynquest.com/blog/how-to-write-a-kids-class-listing-parents-book) walks through each section.

## 4. Run a Waitlist So Cancellations Become Bookings Automatically

Cancellations are a fact of kid life: fevers, birthday party invites, sibling conflicts. The waitlist turns early cancellations into new bookings without any work from you. Turn it on per listing and set a maximum size (the default is 30). When a seat opens, the next family in line gets a 24-hour hold on it, and unused holds pass down the line automatically.

A waitlist also tells you something valuable about demand. A class with 15 enrolled and 12 waitlisted is underpriced or underscheduled: add a second time slot before you raise anything. A class with a waitlist of zero and seats open has a reach problem, not a pricing problem. Treat the list as free market research.

It helps to know the money side of cancellations. When a family gives up part of a booking by cancelling late or not showing up, that share is paid to you: a late cancel under 24 hours before class, or a no-show, pays your full price. One honesty rule goes with it: a no-show may only be recorded for a child who did not come to a class that ran, and recording a false one breaks the Vendor Agreement.

## 5. Reply Within 30 Minutes and Send Post-Class Feedback

You get an email whenever a parent's message sits unread for 30+ minutes. Treat that threshold as your reply target. A parent who asks "is this class okay for a shy 5-year-old?" and gets an answer before dinner often books that night; one who waits two days books somewhere else. Reply speed is also one of the signals search ranking can depend on, along with parent satisfaction, completion and cancellation rates, and profile completeness.

Reviews follow the same logic. Only a parent with a completed booking can review, one review per booking on a 1-to-5-star scale, and families are asked 1 to 72 hours after class. Reply publicly to every review, especially the mixed ones, because parents read how you handle a complaint more carefully than the complaint itself. Name what went wrong, say what changed, and keep it short. Note the quality rule: with 3 or more reviews, an average below 4.0 stars puts a vendor on automatic probation, with listings staying visible until the average returns to 4.0 or above.

After class, send the family short feedback on engagement, focus, social skills, and confidence, plus a note. A parent who reads "Maya shared materials with two new friends today" rebooks and tells friends. For discovery beyond the marketplace itself, our guide to [Google Business Profile for kids' activity businesses](https://orynquest.com/blog/google-business-profile-for-kids-activity-businesses) covers the local search essentials.

## 6. Show Up on Main Street in ORYN Town

Visibility compounds, and one channel works on kids directly. Approved vendors appear as a free storefront on Main Street in ORYN Town, the platform's kids' game world, showing only name, category, and city. Placement is never sold, and you can opt out at any time. When a child recognizes your studio name from the game, your listing starts warm: the "can we try that one?" moment happens before a parent ever opens your page.

The same principle applies everywhere else families find you. Keep your public profile complete with your logo, amenities, and social links, because parents cross-check before they book and a thin profile reads as a thin business. The U.S. Small Business Administration's guidance on local marketing emphasizes keeping your business information consistent across channels, and your profile is the easiest place to get that right: https://www.sba.gov/business-guide.

## 7. Use Your Dashboard to Spot What's Filling and What Isn't

The vendor dashboard and Revenue Report show earnings by month and by listing for completed sessions, plus a 6-month chart, quick insights, and category benchmarks that appear only when at least 5 other vendors share your category. No other vendor's individual numbers are ever shown.

Read the data in pairs. A listing with views but no bookings has a content problem: fix the photos, description, or price. A listing with neither views nor bookings has a discovery problem: fix the category, schedule, or search terms. If Tuesday 4 p.m. art fills and Wednesday 4 p.m. does not, stop running the empty slot and double down on the full one. Schedule discipline beats hope: every term, cut your two emptiest slots and add one more of whatever filled first.

On the money side, there is no fixed payout day. ORYN starts each payout within 30 days after the end of the month the session was completed in, once your bank details are confirmed, and each payout is recorded at the full amount earned with no fee taken out. Keep your own records alongside; you handle your own taxes, and the IRS self-employed business center covers what that means: https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed.

## FAQ

### Does it cost anything to list classes on ORYN Quest?

Joining costs $0 today: no setup fee, no subscription, and nothing taken from the price you set. To apply, you confirm your business carries general liability insurance, and you handle your own taxes. ORYN issues tax forms such as 1099s where the law requires.

### Can I serve families outside Southern California?

Today ORYN Quest is open only for business ZIP codes starting 900 through 935, which covers Southern California. Businesses outside that range can join the vendor waiting list with a name, business, and area, and ORYN emails you when your area opens.

### What happens if a parent cancels at the last minute?

You get paid the share the family gave up. A cancel under 24 hours before class or a no-show pays your full price, and a cancel 24 to 48 hours out pays half. If you cancel the session yourself before it starts, the family gets 100% back and you are not paid, and frequent cancelling can hurt your ranking.

### How do I use ORYN Town, and can I opt out?

Approved vendors appear as a free storefront on Main Street showing only name, category, and city. No prices, contacts, or ads appear, placement is never sold, and you can opt out at any time.

### How fast do I need to reply to parent messages?

Aim for the 30-minute mark, the same threshold at which unread messages trigger an email to you. Reply speed is one of the signals search ranking can depend on, and it is often the difference between a booking and a parent moving on.
